title: Effect of a silent rightward move
statement: Let $x$ and $u$ be binary words, let $q$ be an optional control state, let $q'$ be a control state, let $i$ be a natural number with $i+1\le |x|$, let $h$ be an integer, let $o$ be an output word, and let $e\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Applying the silent action that moves the input head right, moves the work head by $e$, and enters $q'$ to the verifier configuration on $x$ with state $q$, $i$ input bits consumed, work word $u$, work head at $h$, and output $o$, yields the configuration with state $q'$, $i+1$ input bits consumed, the same work word and output, and work head at $h+e$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be an input with $i + 1 \le |x|$. Applying the silent action that moves the
input head right, moves the work head by $e$, and enters state $q'$ to a
non-tautology verifier configuration on $x$ in any state with $i$ input bits consumed, work word
$u$, work head $h$, and output $o$ yields the configuration in state $q'$ with $i+1$
bits consumed, the same $u$ and $o$, and work head $h + e$.
